objective: Allow one release application to carry ordinary delivery units and multiple path-only file-media items through approval, conflict detection, production baseline and current-production views without changing existing delivery-unit behavior.
users: Release applicants registering ordinary artifacts and file paths in one application.
Approvers reviewing complete mixed release application details.
Production managers maintaining deployment results per file path.
Readers querying current production file-media records and release analytics.

requirements.statement: A release application must support simultaneously selected DELIVERY_UNIT and FILE_MEDIA content types, with at least one populated item.
acceptance: Delivery-only, file-only and mixed applications persist and restore the same selected content types.
requirements.source: User selected option 2 and confirmed the page design.
counterexample: The UI forces file media and ordinary delivery units into mutually exclusive applications.

requirements.statement: FILE_MEDIA must support multiple records containing only one file path each and no artifact version.
acceptance: Two distinct paths can be saved in one application; empty, duplicate, oversized or control-character paths are rejected.
requirements.source: User confirmed multiple path-only file-media records.
counterexample: A file-media row requires or derives a version number.

requirements.statement: The server must map each FILE_MEDIA item to fixed delivery unit FILE, name 文件介质 and artifact type FILE while preserving the selected physical subsystem.
acceptance: The client submits only paths and the server creates immutable fixed metadata for each file item.
requirements.source: User request and confirmed data design.
counterexample: A client can persist a file-media item under a non-FILE delivery unit.

requirements.statement: Normalized file path must be the business identity for uniqueness, conflicts, production baseline and production history.
acceptance: Same-window equal paths conflict, distinct paths remain independent, and multiple FILE rows do not overwrite one another.
requirements.source: User confirmed path-level conflict and baseline behavior.
counterexample: All file paths conflict only because their delivery unit code is FILE.

requirements.statement: A previously released equal path must make a later same-window application an additional application while retaining the existing conflict resolution actions.
acceptance: Conflict details include file paths and the new request can cancel old, edit old or continue creating according to existing permissions.
requirements.source: User confirmed the business rules section.
counterexample: File-media conflicts omit historical application details or cannot continue after explicit confirmation.

requirements.statement: Each approved file path must become an independently maintainable production baseline entry.
acceptance: Changing one path result does not alter another path from the same application.
counterexample: One result update changes all FILE paths in the application.

requirements.statement: Successful FILE_MEDIA entries must appear in current production by physical subsystem and normalized path with no version number.
acceptance: Current production shows path, latest successful deployment time and source application, and recalculates after a result reversal.
requirements.source: User explicitly confirmed inclusion in current production.
counterexample: Successful file media disappears from current production or displays a fabricated version.

requirements.statement: Existing ordinary delivery-unit behavior, authorization, workflow status, revision history, audit and stored data must remain compatible.
acceptance: Existing delivery applications remain readable and editable after migration and unauthorized operations remain rejected server-side.
requirements.source: Confirmed compatibility design and repository invariants.
counterexample: Existing delivery records fail to load because new file fields are absent.

requirements.statement: Application detail, conflict, baseline, current production and analytics views must render FILE_MEDIA using its path and item type.
acceptance: No related page renders a blank version code or treats a file path as an ordinary delivery-unit version.
counterexample: Only the create form supports file media while downstream views remain unaware of it.

requirements.statement: The mixed application flow must remain usable without page-level overflow at desktop and required mobile viewports.
acceptance: The drawer and actions are usable at 375x812, 390x844, 430x932 and desktop viewports.
counterexample: Long file paths cover delete or submit actions on mobile.

invariants: One application belongs to one project and one physical subsystem.
Approval remains whole-application rather than per delivery item.
File media never has an artifact version.
FILE is fixed metadata while path is the file-media business identity.
Emergency-window assignment and workflow rules remain unchanged.
Server-side authorization, optimistic locking, revision history and audit remain authoritative.
constraints: Java 17, Spring Boot 3.4.4, Vue 3, TypeScript and existing module boundaries must be preserved.
Flyway migrations are append-only and existing V38/V39 scripts cannot be edited.
Project, physical subsystem and ordinary delivery-unit option sources remain frontend mocks.
No production access, secret reads or external filesystem access is permitted.
Frontend must reuse existing release form and delivery-showcase responsive patterns.
non_goals: Reading, uploading, validating or previewing the real file behind a path.
Adding file version, checksum, size, host, environment or directory browsing.
Building project, subsystem or delivery-unit master data services.
Changing workflow definitions, window policy, version-type policy or menu permissions.
Refactoring unrelated release or platform modules.

selected_approach.name: Extend the unified release delivery-item model
selected_approach.reason: File media shares the existing application, approval and production state machine; a stable item key allows path-level identity without duplicating transactions and audit behavior.

alternatives.name: Separate application and production tables for file media
alternatives.rejected_because: It duplicates conflict, baseline, result maintenance and analytics logic and raises consistency risk.

alternatives.name: Separate write table with a unified projection
alternatives.rejected_because: It requires additional projection and cross-table transaction complexity without enough benefit for the current scope.

inside: Release application UI and API DTOs
Release application validation, persistence and conflict identity
Production baseline and current-production persistence and queries
Append-only release schema migration and focused tests

components.name: ReleaseApplicationDrawer
components.responsibility: Edit selected content types, ordinary deliveries and dynamic file-path rows with responsive validation.

components.name: ReleaseApplicationService
components.responsibility: Normalize paths, generate immutable file metadata and stable item keys, validate and resolve conflict/additional semantics.

components.name: ReleaseApplicationStore
components.responsibility: Persist revisioned unified delivery items and query conflicts by stable item key.

components.name: ReleaseProductionService and Store
components.responsibility: Create independent file baseline entries, maintain results and calculate current production by subsystem and item key.

components.name: Release analytics
components.responsibility: Include FILE item type in aggregates and drill-down rows without fabricating versions.

components.name: Flyway V46
components.responsibility: Add and backfill item identity fields, nullable file-only version support and compatible unique indexes.

interfaces.name: Release application write DTO
interfaces.contract: Preserve deliveries and add fileMedia containing path-only records; server owns fixed FILE metadata.

interfaces.name: Release item read DTOs
interfaces.contract: Expose itemType and filePath so consumers choose path or version rendering explicitly.

interfaces.name: Stable item key
interfaces.contract: UNIT:<code> for ordinary items and FILE:<SHA-256(trimmed-path)> for file media.

data_flows.input: Ordinary deliveries plus zero or more file paths
data_flows.output: A draft or submitted mixed release application
Audited baseline rows and current production records

error_handling.condition: No ordinary delivery and no file-media path
error_handling.behavior: Reject save or submit with a field-level business message and no partial write.
error_handling.recovery: Add at least one item and retry.

error_handling.behavior: Reject before persistence and identify the invalid path.
error_handling.recovery: Correct or remove the path and retry.

error_handling.behavior: Return full conflict facts without starting workflow approval.
error_handling.recovery: Cancel old, edit old or explicitly continue creating.
Reload conflict facts and decide again.

error_handling.behavior: Stop backend startup and preserve the database for diagnosis.
error_handling.recovery: Restore backup if needed, correct with an append-only migration and restart.

security: Treat paths as escaped business text and never execute or resolve them on the server.
Retain existing server-side RBAC, entity authorization and audit for every write.
performance: Index fixed-length item keys rather than 1024-character paths.
Keep conflict and production queries tenant-, window-, status- and item-key bounded.
compatibility: Preserve existing deliveries DTO semantics and backfill every old row as DELIVERY_UNIT.
Allow null artifact version only for FILE_MEDIA.
operations: Run V46 against a backed-up isolated database and verify repeat startup.
Keep mock synchronization disabled while validating manually created release data.
Never downgrade Flyway; use a later compensating migration for schema recovery.

verification_strategy.signal: Application service and persistence tests pass for delivery-only, file-only, mixed, invalid and migrated records.
verification_strategy.method: Focused ccb-release unit and schema contract tests.

verification_strategy.signal: Equal path conflicts and additional detection are stable while distinct paths remain independent.
verification_strategy.method: Conflict service tests and real submit API flow.

verification_strategy.signal: Each path has an independent baseline result and current-production history recalculates correctly.
verification_strategy.method: Production service tests and real approval/deployment API flow.

verification_strategy.signal: Every related view renders file media by path without overflow or fabricated version text.
verification_strategy.method: Frontend production build and browser checks at desktop, 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932.

verification_strategy.signal: Repository governance, scope, full Maven tests and frontend build pass with no unresolved negative feedback.
verification_strategy.method: Governance scripts, scope check, mvn test, npm build and convergence review.

assumptions.text: A file path is an internal business identifier and does not need filesystem resolution.
assumptions.basis: The user requested path-only storage and no file upload behavior.
assumptions.falsifier: A later requirement asks the platform to verify, read or deploy the referenced file directly.

assumptions.text: Path case and slash differences can denote distinct targets, so normalization trims only surrounding whitespace.
assumptions.basis: No target operating-system or shared-storage canonicalization rule was requested.
assumptions.falsifier: A platform-wide canonical path convention is supplied.

assumptions.text: Fixed FILE metadata does not require a corresponding option in the frontend master-data mock.
assumptions.basis: The server owns fixed file-media metadata.
assumptions.falsifier: The future master-data service requires referential validation for every delivery-unit snapshot.

decisions.decision: Ordinary delivery units and file media may coexist in one application.
File media supports multiple path-only records and no version number.
decisions.reason: This is the explicitly confirmed business input.

decisions.decision: Conflict, baseline and production identity is path-level while fixed delivery metadata remains FILE.
decisions.reason: Different file paths must not overwrite or conflict with one another.

decisions.decision: Extend the existing unified delivery-item model.
decisions.reason: It reuses the current workflow, audit and production state machine with the smallest coherent persistence change.

risks.risk: Existing code assumes delivery_unit_code uniquely identifies every application and production item.
risks.impact: Multiple FILE paths could overwrite, conflict or share results.
risks.mitigation: Introduce and consistently use a stable item key, then regress every code-based query.

risks.risk: Nullable artifact versions leak into ordinary delivery behavior.
risks.impact: Invalid ordinary deliveries or blank downstream displays.
risks.mitigation: Enforce null only for FILE_MEDIA in service validation and tests.

risks.risk: Unique-key migration fails on existing data.
risks.impact: Backend startup fails and release data becomes unavailable.
risks.mitigation: Back up and validate V46 on the isolated local database, stop on failure and never skip Flyway.

risks.risk: Mixed application content overflows the mobile drawer.
risks.impact: Users cannot review paths or reach actions.
risks.mitigation: Use vertical responsive sections, wrap long paths and verify all required viewports.

approval.evidence: The user approved all four design sections and, after the persisted design was presented for review, explicitly requested implementation to start.
